lines.text: Do you know why people are using Orbi Transfer?
Picture this. The lights drop, the whole crowd screams, and you catch the encore. Perfectly.
And now your friends are all yelling the same thing: send it to me!
But chat apps crush it into a blurry mess, and email just says: file too big.
So you drop the clip into Orbi Transfer, set a code, and that's it. Sent.
Every friend around you gets it in seconds. Full quality!
Wait. How does that actually work?
Think of your clip as a song. Your phone locks it in a guitar case, and the code is the key. It never leaves your hand.
Then the song breaks into notes, and they all fly out at once, like a whole band playing together. That's why it's so fast.
The notes wait backstage, behind a locked door. No code? Nobody gets in.
Then Orbi sends a light wave across your part of the city, like a stadium wave. It knows the area. Never your seat.
Your friend types the code, the notes fly back, snap together, and the whole song plays!
And thirty minutes later? The stage goes dark. Everything's gone. No account. No trace.
Orbi Transfer dot com. Try it before the next encore.
